subject: Pilot kickoff: rightsizing GPU options + performance validation plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@spectraai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-08T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot kickoff: rightsizing GPU options + performance validation plan

Hi Sam / Maya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can scope a focused dedicated-capacity pilot that answers your latency and throughput risk questions. I pulled the actionable items into three buckets: targets, pilot configuration, and deliverables.

Targets (from discovery)
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms for 512-token responses (interactive UI), p95 <= 850ms for 2048-token batch generation (backend jobs)
- Concurrency: steady-state 10 concurrent user sessions with spikes to 25 for short periods
- Throughput: target sustained token-generation rate equivalent to ~120k tokens/minute across the pool during peak
- Streaming: token-level streaming with sub-100ms first-byte for short responses (under 200 tokens)

Pilot configuration (recommended start)
- Duration: 7 business days (stretch to 14 if you want broader workload coverage)
- Reserved throughput: provision for 120k tokens/minute peak, with 20% headroom (150k tokens/minute) configured as burstable capacity
- GPU contenders to validate: NVIDIA H100 (80GB, fp16 + 4-bit quant) vs NVIDIA A100 (80GB, fp16 + 8-bit dynamic) — we’ll run identical models and quant setups on both for apples-to-apples comparisons
- Concurrency strategy: mix of dedicated worker slots + autoscale buffer; target 10 steady slots, 25 burstable slots
- Telemetry: token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, memory pressure, KV cache hit rates, prefix caching savings

Deliverables from Redwood
- Pilot performance matrix (A100 vs H100) with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens for each config
- Runbook for warm pool sizing and recommended batching/latency settings to meet p95 targets
- Shared Drive with perf-bench-plan.md and pilot-matrix.xlsx (see attachments)

Next steps
1) Let me know whether 7 days is enough or you prefer 14.
2) Ben / Karthik — can you confirm feasibility of the H100 test harness + suggested quant profiles? I listed a baseline below.
3) Sam — if the targets above miss anything, flag it and I’ll adjust the plan. If that looks good, I’ll schedule a kickoff next week (Mon or Tue preferred).

Baseline quant/profile suggestion (for Ben)
- H100: fp16 baseline + run 4-bit quant (q4) for the main model variant; try q4+KV compression for long contexts
- A100: fp16 baseline + 8-bit dynamic quant (q8d) to minimize accuracy delta

Thanks — feel free to mark up the Drive doc if you want any additional checkpoints.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff: rightsizing GPU options + performance validation plan

Thanks Tessa — this looks spot on and aligns with what we discussed. Couple of clarifications from our side:

- Concurrency: the 10 steady sessions are realistic. Our client web app multiplexes multiple prompts per session (avg 1.6 requests/sec per session) so plan accordingly.
- Streaming: token-level streaming is a hard requirement for the UI; first-byte under 100ms is a must for short prompts (<=150 tokens).
- Model size: we plan to validate with a 13B conversational model currently in-house (we can share weights for a trimmed-down validation build).
- Security/procurement: we need a short SOW for pilot procurement folks; budget cap is $45k for the pilot.

If H100 gives material latency headroom at a similar cost profile to A100 with q8, we’ll prefer H100 for production.

We’re good for a Monday kickoff (Aug 14) if that works on your end.

—Sam

Head of Product, SpectraAI

On Tue, Aug 8, 2028 at 09:43 Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Baseline quant/profile suggestion (for Ben)
> - H100: fp16 baseline + run 4-bit quant (q4) for the main model variant; try q4+KV compression for long contexts
> - A100: fp16 baseline + 8-bit dynamic quant (q8d) to minimize accuracy delta

Quick engineering read — high level: feasible. Below are concrete bench steps and immediate recommendations so procurement and the product team have clear expectations.

Bench plan highlights (what we’ll run during pilot)
1) Throughput sweep: measure tokens/sec and latency curves across batch sizes (1,2,4,8) and concurrency (5,10,25) for both GPUs and both quant modes
2) Streaming tail checks: measure first-byte latency for short responses (<=150 tokens) at 10/25 concurrent sessions with realistic prompt mix
3) KV and prefix caching: validate 30-minute session reuse scenario to quantify cache hit rate impact on p95
4) Cost per 1k tokens: capture raw infra cost + estimated Redwood serving overhead for each config

Preliminary perf expectations (13B model; trimmed weights)
- H100 (fp16): p95 interactive ~180–260ms (512 tokens), p99 ~450–650ms depending on batching
- H100 (q4): p95 can be within 15–25% of fp16 with proper kernel selection + KV cache enabled
- A100 (fp16): p95 interactive ~230–320ms
- A100 (q8d): p95 may approach H100 fp16 for short contexts but will widen with longer contexts and heavy concurrency

Sizing & reserved throughput recommendation
- Reserve a pool sized for sustained 120k tokens/minute (your peak) + 20% headroom; map this to X H100 instances (we’ll provide the exact instance count after initial microbench)
- Warm pool: maintain a small set of hot workers (10–15% of steady capacity) to keep KV warmed and reduce first-byte jitter

Procurement / SOW notes
- We can produce a 1-page SOW: scope, pilot duration, success criteria (p95<=350ms for 512 tokens, streaming first-byte <=100ms), budget cap, and data handling terms.
- Attachments: pilot-matrix.xlsx (matrix template), perf-bench-plan.md (detailed steps & scripts).

I’ll start drafting the SOW and the perf scripts this afternoon. Tessa — if Monday (Aug 14) is kickoff, engineering should be ready to spin the harness next week.

—Ben
